objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. A Chinese-Thai neighbourhood shrine hall. A pale stone plinth with quoins at the wall corners and a tripod censer on the porch floor; red-lacquer side walls running the full depth to the front, a 3.5 m deep open colonnade inside them in front of a door wall with a closed central door pair and two open doorways; eight round red columns on stone drums, the two centre front ones wrapped in gilt dragons; a sooted bracket beam with gilt relief panels under the eaves; ten conical incense coils hung across the open front; and over it all a heavy low green-glazed xieshan roof -- concave long slopes, hip skirt, vertical red pediments, swallow-tail ridge horns, four flying corners and a pair of guardian beasts on a tall ridge bar.

reasoning: The registry notes open with a WARNING rather than a description -- it must not be built with the profile of a Thai wat -- and the proxy says what it IS: a xieshan hip-and-gable, one continuous concave slope from eaves to ridge on the long faces, a shallow hip skirt on the ends that stops at a vertical pediment, and horns at every end and corner.
That roof cannot be extruded or lathed. It is generated as subdivided rings climbing from the eaves to the ridge, with the long-slope profile read straight off the proxy depth map.

The two features the notes call out for recognition -- dragon-wrapped columns and hanging incense coils -- are both real geometry; the tile courses, eaves caps, soot and staining the plate resolves at prop distance are post-construction canvases on textureless materials.
Action readiness is minimal: static landmark geometry, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Three repetition systems, a subdivided swept roof and five canvases against a twelve-draw-call ceiling. The ten incense coils alone would be ten of the twelve as separate meshes.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 8.70 x 9.20 x 12.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=16000 triangles, <=12 draw calls, <=8 materials, <=32 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares, +Y up. The OPEN FRONT faces +X and the long 12 m axis is Z. The building is offset under its roof exactly as the proxy reads it -- front wall at x = +3.52, back wall at x = -2.76, plinth +3.68 / -2.88 -- so the front eaves overhang 0.6 m and the back 1.4 m, which is what the plate shows behind the colonnade.

silhouette.description: A low pale plinth flush with the walls, a red body the full length and depth of the plinth with an open colonnade cut into its front half, and a roof that is nearly half the height and wider than everything under it. The silhouette events are all in the roof: the concave sweep from a steep ridge out to shallow flaring eaves that lift into the four corners, the vertical pediments inset from the hip ends, the tall ridge bar and the two swallow-tail horns at 1.0 H.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: v2 (2026-08-28): re-declared from the Meshy proxy bbox, 1.90 x 1.45 x 1.38 units = long : h : short = 1 : 0.764 : 0.726, at the kept 12 m length: h = 9.2 m, across = 8.7 m. In the model the long axis is Z (walls at z = +-5.01, eaves at +-5.93, ridge-horn tips at +-6.4), the open front is +X, and the building is NOT centred under its roof: the proxy puts the front wall at +0.383 H (x = 3.52) and the back wall at -0.30 H (x = -2.76), with the eaves at +-0.45 H (x = +-4.14) and the flying corners pushed to +-4.5. y spans 0 to 9.17, the tip of a ridge-end horn.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to long:h:short = 1 : 0.764 : 0.731, and v2 adopts that as the declaration. Four orthographic depth maps of the proxy (scratch/_mon/front.mjs, +-x and +-z) were column-scanned: the long-slope profile at x~0 is the roof section used verbatim (eave lip 0.615 H at z 0.45 H, apex 0.84 H, concave 18 -> 33 deg); the end map reads the pediment as a vertical face at 0.445 H from 0.69 H up; band 8 puts all surface within +-0.05 H of the ridge line (the tall ridge bar); the front map puts the wall ends at +-0.545 H on the front plane and the door wall at mid depth. Area-weighted band comparison after rebuilding on those numbers: mean |delta width| 0.045, |delta depth| 0.044 of height (v1 was 0.157 / 0.116), no band over 0.09 except band 9, where the candidate horn tips reach 0.77 of height along the ridge against the proxy 0.94.

featureReviews.notes: The preamble's curledHorn samples a sine and built spikes; spiralHorn() turns the heading past vertical so the ridge ends curl back over as the plate's do. Held at 0.88: the tails are swept box segments, not the flat fan the plate shows, and the corner curls are short.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Six components and three repetition systems: 9 of 12. The whole roof -- surface, ridge, ten horns, boards and beasts -- is ONE submission; the fascia is a second only because its cap canvas needs its own clamped texture; the two dragons and five gilt panels are a third.

materials.note: pale covers the plinth, quoins, censer AND the eight drums; red covers the body, pediments and the eight shafts; green and eave are the same glaze under two canvases. Seven of eight, one in hand, and every one is a genuinely different finish or a different texture on it.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 8,012 of 16,000. The swept roof is 19 rings x 8 per side; the two dragon tubes are 1,024 triangles each; the rest is boxes, lathes and cones.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A swept xieshan surface from subdivided rings on a measured profile table, a helical tube, spiral horns, lathes and boxes. The roof is the one shape in this batch no existing helper could express -- not an extrusion, which gives vertical ends the full length, and not a lathe, which cannot be rectangular in plan.

Three InstancedMesh systems carry 26 of the prop's discrete parts. Two of them share one placement schedule and differ only in material and shape, which is what a column and its stone base actually are.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. Five post-construction Canvas 2D tiles on the CPU canvas path -- tile courses (2 m), eaves caps (clamped band), lacquer soot streaks (2 m), stone staining (2 m), coil grooves -- are bound as map + bumpMap AFTER construction, so each material keeps its measured albedo as the multiplicand; under Node the factory runs without them. 4.6 MB texture VRAM, 72 ms factory.
